facts.evidence: GAAP revenue from continuing operations was $17.2 billion, up 1% year-over-year
Operating (non-GAAP) diluted EPS was $2.93, up 5% year-over-year.
Software revenue was $7.8 billion, up 5% year-over-year
The company now expects full-year 2026 constant currency revenue growth in the range of 4–5%.
Full-year 2026 free cash flow is expected to increase by about $1 billion year-over-year.
The company returned $1.6 billion to shareholders in dividends during the second quarter.
Infrastructure revenue was $3.8 billion, down 7% year-over-year, with Distributed Infrastructure up 37% and IBM Z down 42%.

claims.claim: GAAP revenue from continuing operations was $17.2 billion, up 1% year-over-year.
claims.note: Income statement summary: GAAP revenue 17.2B, year/year 1.

claims.claim: GAAP net income was $2.2 billion, down 1% year-over-year.
claims.note: Summary table: GAAP net income 2.2B, year/year (1).

claims.claim: Operating (non-GAAP) pre-tax income was $3.3 billion, up 3% year-over-year.
claims.note: Summary table operating row: pre-tax income 3.3B, year/year 3.

claims.claim: Operating (non-GAAP) diluted EPS was $2.93, up 5% year-over-year.
claims.note: Summary table operating row: diluted EPS 2.93, year/year 5.

claims.claim: GAAP gross profit margin was 57.7%, down 1.0 point year-over-year.
claims.note: Summary table: GAAP gross profit margin 57.7, year/year (1.0) pts.

claims.claim: Operating (non-GAAP) gross profit margin was 59.4%, down 0.7 points year-over-year.
claims.note: Summary table operating row: 59.4, year/year (0.7) pts.

claims.claim: The company generated $2.6 billion in net cash from operating activities in the second quarter, up $0.9 billion year-over-year.
claims.note: Cash Flow section states $2.6 billion, up $0.9 billion year to year.

claims.claim: Software revenue was $7.8 billion, up 5% year-over-year.
claims.note: Segment results: Software revenues of $7.8 billion, up 5 percent.

claims.claim: Software growth was driven by 11% growth in Hybrid Cloud (Red Hat) and 19% growth in Data.
claims.note: Release lists Hybrid Cloud (Red Hat) up 11 percent and Data up 19 percent within Software.

claims.claim: Infrastructure revenue was $3.8 billion, down 7% year-over-year.
claims.note: Segment results: Infrastructure revenues of $3.8 billion, down 7 percent.

claims.claim: Within Infrastructure, Distributed Infrastructure was up 37% and IBM Z was down 42%.
claims.note: Segment results list Distributed Infrastructure up 37 percent and IBM Z down 42 percent.

claims.claim: Consulting revenue was $5.3 billion, flat year-over-year and up 1% at constant currency.
claims.note: Segment results: Consulting revenues of $5.3 billion, flat, up 1 percent at constant currency.

claims.claim: Power and Storage within Distributed Infrastructure grew at a record pace, building an order backlog of nearly $500 million.
claims.note: Operational Focus Areas states Power and Storage grew at a record pace with backlog of nearly $500 million.

claims.claim: The company now expects full-year 2026 constant currency revenue growth in the range of 4–5%.
claims.note: Full-Year 2026 Expectations state constant currency revenue growth of four-to-five percent.

claims.claim: Full-year 2026 free cash flow is expected to increase by about $1 billion year-over-year.
claims.note: Release: company continues to expect full-year free cash flow to increase by about $1 billion year-over-year.

claims.claim: The company expects improved pre-tax income margin expansion for the full year.
claims.note: Release: 'The company now expects improved pre-tax income margin expansion for the full year.'

claims.claim: IBM ended Q2 2026 with $8.2 billion in cash, restricted cash and marketable securities, down $6.3 billion from year-end 2025.
claims.note: Cash and Balance Sheet section states exactly this.

claims.claim: Total debt, including IBM Financing debt of $13.0 billion, was $62.0 billion, up $0.7 billion year-to-date.
claims.note: Cash and Balance Sheet section states exactly this.

claims.claim: The company returned $1.6 billion to shareholders in dividends during the second quarter.
claims.note: Cash and Balance Sheet section states exactly this.

claims.claim: IBM invested $10.5 billion in acquisitions this year.
claims.note: Release: 'The company invested $10.5 billion in acquisitions this year.'

claims.claim: IBM plans to invest $10 billion in quantum computing over the next five years.
claims.note: Release says 'more than $10 billion in quantum over the next five years'; brief's flat '$10 billion' drops the 'more than' floor, a minor understatement.
